basics.name: Chijioke Ugwuanyi
basics.label: AI Safety Researcher
basics.summary: AI safety researcher with 7+ years of software engineering experience. At the Jinesis AI Lab (University of Toronto), I designed and ran AF-Arena, a multi-axis evaluation arena for alignment faking in frontier LLMs — accepted as an oral at the ICML 2026 Workshop on Agents in the Wild and under review at NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations & Datasets Track) — and co-authored AM-Bench (submitted to NeurIPS 2026). Transitioning fully into technical AI safety research.

work.name: Jinesis AI Lab, University of Toronto
highlights: Designed AF-Arena, a 5-axis evaluation arena for alignment faking in frontier LLMs; evaluated 9 models (GPT-5 series, Gemini 3, Claude 4.6, DeepSeek-R1, Grok 4.20) across 54,000 trials. Accepted as an oral at the ICML 2026 Workshop on Agents in the Wild; under review at NeurIPS 2026 (Evaluations & Datasets Track)

Co-authored AM-Bench (submitted to NeurIPS 2026; with B. Schölkopf, Z. Jin et al.), a unified taxonomy and evaluation suite for agentic misalignment grounded in the fraud triangle (35 scenarios, 7 industries, 11 frontier models); built the modular evaluation harness, scenario set, and rationalization-scoring pass

Conducted an 8,400-trial ablation study showing that elicitation conditions are axis-dependent: monitoring is necessary on both ablated axes, while explicit training criteria are additionally required on Axis E (sycophancy) but dispensable on Axis K (goal-guarding)
Ran a 62,400-trial prompt-based mitigation sweep; identified and named three novel failure modes: behavioral masking, meta-alignment-faking, and self-aware alignment faking

work.name: Independent Research — Agentic Misalignment & Alignment Faking
highlights: Extended Lynch et al. (2025) agentic misalignment study across 22 models from 8B to frontier; found blackmail/leak/murder rates vary by model family and system-prompt framing, not model size, with DeepSeek highly vulnerable while latest OpenAI/Anthropic models stay near-zero (published on LessWrong)
Replicated Koorndijk (2025), showing differential compliance in Llama 3 8B stems from lexical prompt sensitivity rather than genuine strategic reasoning (published on LessWrong)
Attempted replication of Betley et al.'s emergent misalignment work; produced a negative result where 4-bit QLoRA fine-tuning caused code mode collapse rather than the reported persona shift

publications.name: AF-Arena: An Evaluation Arena for Multi-Axis Alignment Faking in Frontier Language Models

publications.summary: Ugwuanyi, C. (first author), Zhang, T.J., Schölkopf, B., Jin, Z. — Tests whether frontier LLMs fake alignment across five behavioral axes; characterizes three novel failure modes of prompt-based mitigations.

publications.name: From 8B to Frontier: How System Prompts Control Whether AI Agents Blackmail, Leak, and Kill
publications.summary: Susceptibility to agentic misalignment across 22 models is driven by model family and system-prompt framing rather than model size.

publications.name: Blackmail at 8 Billion Parameters: Agentic Misalignment in Sub-Frontier Models
publications.summary: Blackmail rates in sub-frontier open-weight models vary dramatically by model family rather than parameter count.

publications.name: Replication of Koorndijk (2025): Differential Compliance May Reflect Prompt Sensitivity, Not Strategic Reasoning
publications.summary: Differential compliance observed in Llama 3 8B is better explained by lexical prompt sensitivity than by genuine strategic reasoning.
